This feature needs the Display over other apps permission to work. Please turn that on first, then turn this on. If something stops working, restart the app.

 Turning this on lets Mindstop do these things for you:
1. Block apps
2. Block short form content
3. Block websites and keywords
4. Focus Mode
5. Hide parts of an app's screen that distract you
6. See how long you spend in each app
7. Count how much short form content you scroll, and show the count in a floating overlay
8. See which websites you visit and for how long

 Mindstop needs accessibility access to see which app, website, or screen you are on, so it can block it the way you set and keep your usage stats. Without this, none of it can work.

 Mindstop never shares anything without your permission.

Mindstop needs this to show a calm pause screen on top of distracting apps when you open them. Without it, Mindstop cannot place anything over those apps to help you stop and think.
🛡️ Open Source: Think of Mindstop like a restaurant with an open kitchen. The whole codebase is public, so anyone can check that Mindstop is not doing anything sneaky. There are no closed doors here.
Mindstop needs this to stay running in the background so your blocks keep working, and to gently remind you of your goals. Without it, Android can stop Mindstop and your blocks may fail.

🛡️ Not a Data Broker: Many apps hide their code because they make money by harvesting your data. Mindstop keeps all its code public, so you can check yourself that nothing is quietly sending your information away.

Mindstop needs this to notice when you open a blocked app and show the blocker screen. It also uses it to count your screen time and how many reels you scroll. Without it, Mindstop cannot work at all.

🛡️ Transparency for Deep Access: This is a powerful permission, which is why being open source matters so much. You do not have to take Mindstop at its word. The global community has reviewed its public code and confirmed it only blocks apps and tracks usage.

resources.string: Ride out a strong craving instead of fighting it.

A craving is like a wave. It rises, peaks, and fades, usually within a few minutes. Urge surfing helps you wait it out. You rate the craving, think about it for a moment, then play a calm puzzle or move your body for 3 minutes. Then you rate it again and see how much it dropped.
Offer help after 3 unlocks in a row

Getting past the block screen again and again is a sign of a strong craving. After 3 unlocks in a row, the block screen offers help even if the button above is off. Tapping Cancel starts the count over.

resources.string: Get your notifications together at set times, not all day long.

Notifications pull you back to your phone all day. With this on, Mindstop holds them when they come in and gives them back together at the times you pick. For example, at 9 in the morning, 1 in the afternoon, and 6 in the evening.

Calls, alarms, and ongoing notifications like music or maps always come through. A notification may make a short sound before Mindstop holds it. If you turn this off, notifications that are already held still come back at the next delivery time.
Mindstop needs notification access to hold your notifications until the times you pick. Mindstop does not read, save, or send them anywhere.
